info.title: kling/videos-avatar-image2video
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "kling/videos-avatar-image2video", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Generate an avatar video from an image and exactly one audio source: audio_id or sound_file.

example.prompt: The presenter smiles and gestures towards the camera.

audio_id.description: Audio ID Generated via TTS API. Only supports 2-300 second audio generated within the last 30 days. Either audio_id or sound_file must be provided (mutually exclusive).

callback_url.description: The callback notification address for the result of this task.

external_task_id.description: Customized Task ID. Must be unique within a single user account.

image.description: Avatar Reference Image. Supports Base64 encoding or image URL. Supported formats: .jpg/.jpeg/.png. Max 10MB, min 300px width/height, aspect ratio between 1:2.5 and 2.5:1.

prompt.description: Positive text prompt. Can define avatar actions, emotions, and camera movements.

sound_file.description: Sound File. Supports Base64-encoded audio or accessible audio URL. Accepted formats: .mp3/.wav/.m4a/.aac (max 5MB), 2-300 seconds. Either audio_id or sound_file must be provided (mutually exclusive).

enabled.description: Whether to generate watermarked results simultaneously.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Kling v1 VIDEO models: the terminal `GET /v1/videos/{operation}/{id}` task-query document, forwarded unchanged. Every Kling v1 operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL, each polled on `<submit path>/:id` — the four this component covers, `/v1/videos/text2video`, `/v1/videos/image2video`, `/v1/videos/omni-video` and `/v1/videos/avatar/image2video`, and the lip-sync and video-extend siblings documented separately alike — and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{code, message, request_id, data.task_id}` handle the underlying `/proxy/kling/*` submit answers with.
The generated video's download URL is at `data.task_result.videos[].url`. Read the ELEMENT field, not the `videos` container: `KlingVideoResult` is `{id, url, watermark_url, duration}`, so a one-element list carrying an id and a duration and no URL is a non-empty array holding nothing playable. `data.task_result.videos[].watermark_url` is the same asset under Kling's hotlink-protection form and counts as a result; `routerpollstate.classifyKling` draws exactly that line, and a `succeed` carrying neither is `success_without_output` rather than a finished generation.
`data.task_status` is Kling's own four-value vocabulary — `submitted`, `processing`, `succeed`, `failed` — and the terminal success spells it `succeed`, NOT `succeeded`. The `kling/kling-3.0-turbo` sibling (`KlingV2RouterOutput`) says `succeeded` and carries an entirely different document; the two vocabularies are deliberately not folded together.
Four operations share this component because they share this document, and the ids are grouped by operation in the list above: text2video is the family's primary, so `kling/kling-v1-5` and `kling/kling-v2-1` — the two ids text2video's allowlist does not admit — resolve onto image2video, and `kling/kling-v3-omni` and `kling/kling-video-o1` resolve onto omni-video. The last id is a route-slug model — `kling/videos-avatar-image2video`, the only id on its own operation. Its document is typed separately in the v1 contract (`KlingAvatarResponse`) but declares the same property set as `KlingQueryTaskResponse`, envelope and `data.task_result.videos[]` leaf alike, which is why it is documented here rather than as a near-identical component of its own. Its two route-slug siblings are NOT: `kling/videos-lip-sync` and `kling/videos-video-extend` answer a strictly NARROWER envelope and are authored by `KlingLipSyncRouterOutput` and `KlingVideoExtendRouterOutput`. `kling/videos-avatar-image2video` publishes its own example, on its own model page; the eleven generation-id pages carry the shared text2video one.

KlingAvatarMode.description: Video generation mode. std: Standard Mode (cost-effective), pro: Professional Mode (longer duration, higher quality).

created_at.description: Task creation time, Unix timestamp in milliseconds

task_status_msg.description: Task status information, displaying the failure reason when the task fails

updated_at.description: Task update time, Unix timestamp in milliseconds

watermark_url.description: URL for generated video with watermark, hotlink protection format
